scenes.line1: Which join speeds up Spark jobs?
scenes.say: Which join type can make your Spark job faster: broadcast or sort-merge?

scenes.label: Broadcast
scenes.sub: Sends small table to all executors, skips shuffles.
scenes.say: Broadcast joins send a small table to every executor, avoiding costly shuffles.

scenes.label: Sort-Merge
scenes.sub: Shuffles and sorts both tables, best for large data.
scenes.say: Sort-merge joins shuffle and sort both tables, which works better for large datasets.
Use broadcast joins for small dimension tables. Sort-merge is for large fact tables and needs more resources.

scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
result = df1.join(broadcast(df2), 'id')
scenes.say: You can force a broadcast join by wrapping your DataFrame with the broadcast function.

scenes.question: Why avoid shuffles in Spark joins?
scenes.right: Shuffles use disk and network I/O, slowing jobs.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Why avoid shuffles in Spark joins? Because shuffles use disk and network input-output, slowing down your jobs.
